subject: On-prem blueprint: GPU node pools, storage tiering, and egress controls
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@greenfield.ai>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: opslead@greenfield.ai
Date: 2027-03-20T09:12:05-07:00
Subject: Design rundown: on-prem constraints & PVC strategy

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for taking this call earlier. I wanted to summarize our primary constraints so you and your infra folks can sketch a proposal before the formal design review: 

- Environment: air-gapped customer datacenter (no outbound internet), VMWare-based hardware layer, 10Gb internal fabric.
- Compliance: logs and audit trail must be retained on-site for 365 days; ability to rotate keys via our HSM.
- GPUs: initial cluster will run inference on 8x A100s (customer prefers one pod per GPU) with planned quarterly scale to 16 GPUs.
- Multi-tenancy: single cluster serving multiple product teams; strict namespace isolation required.
- Storage: model artifacts ~25TB (mostly reads), ephemeral KV/cache I/O heavy (low latency).
- Backup/DR: nightly backups for artifacts; RTO target 4 hours, RPO 1 hour for critical caches.
- Network: egress must be restricted; outbound to Redwood private registry via controlled HTTP proxy is acceptable.

Attached: Greenfield-Infra-constraints.pdf (hardware inventory + compliance checklist). Can you confirm recommended node pool shapes, storage topology (local NVMe vs replicated block), and whether Redwood recommends a CSI-backed replicated store (Rook/Ceph, long-term) vs customer NAS? Also flag any gotchas for air-gapped installs (registry sync, CRI, kernel modules).

Appreciate a short list of open questions we should answer before the design review.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Head of Infrastructure
Greenfield Robotics

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-20T11:05:22-07:00
Subject: Re: Design rundown: on-prem constraints & PVC strategy

Maya—

Thanks for the clear constraints doc, that helps a lot. Quick answers up front and then a short proposal.

Top-level recommendations (short):
- Node pools: dedicated GPU node pool (tainted + nodeSelector) with 1 pod per GPU; separate pool for model artifact storage/IO services; control plane (3 masters) on dedicated hardware.
- Storage tiers: two-tier model: (1) ephemeral NVMe on GPU nodes for KV/cache (localTxn, no replication) and (2) replicated block storage for model artifacts (Ceph/Rook or customer SAN via CSI).
- Registry & air-gap: we recommend a mirrored private registry you seed via signed tarballs; automated sync job runs over one-way USB/secure transfer.
- Networking/egress: NAT gateway on a perimeter jump host; only specific egress to Redwood registry/proxy allowed; iptables + Calico egress rules for namespace-level controls.

Open questions we need answered before the formal design doc:
1) Expected steady-state QPS and peak concurrent sessions (token/sec) per model.
2) Acceptable trade for cache RPO (can we accept cache loss on node restart?).
3) Preference for in-cluster replicated storage (Rook/Ceph) vs external SAN/NAS (vendor + model).
4) Rack-level topology for GPU nodes (are GPUs on separate racks or distributed?).

I'll attach a short checklist and a proposed time for a technical sync. Marissa and Dev, please add any configuration snippets and storage notes (esp. OSD sizing and PV reclaim behavior).

Attachments: redwood-onprem-checklist.xlsx (checklist + minimal systemd scripts for registry mirror).

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@greenfield.ai>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-21T08:39:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Design rundown: on-prem constraints & PVC strategy

Maya / team—

Adding a technical matrix and concrete configuration guidance from the infra side. High level followed by examples.

Recommendations (detailed):
- Control plane: 3 dedicated master nodes (VMs or baremetal) with etcd quorum distributed across two racks if possible; etcd disk: mirrored NVMe with iSCSI fallback.

- GPU node pool: 1 GPU per pod, GPU node taint: redwood/gpu=true:NoSchedule; kubelet args: --feature-gates=DevicePlugins=true; use NVIDIA device plugin with resourceName nvidia.com/gpu. If MIG is in play, we recommend 1:1 mapping to simplify scheduler.

- Storage topology: 3-tier approach:
  * Tier 0 (ephemeral cache): Local NVMe on GPU nodes mounted via local PersistentVolume (fast, no replication). Use tmpfs for hottest KV if memory allows.
  * Tier 1 (model artifacts, read-heavy): Replicated block via Rook/Ceph (CephFS or RBD) with at least 3 OSD nodes; OSD sizing: plan for 2x working set + 1x replica factor; use cephfs for shared POSIX mounts, rbd for block attachments to model servers.
  * Tier 2 (archives/backups): External SAN or tape gateway; nightly rsync of artifacts, consider incremental snapshots with borg/restic to HSM-backed tape.

- CSI & performance: use the Rook operator pinned to control namespace; tune rados settings for small object read-heavy workloads (op_threads, filestore settings). For slow networks, enable async writes and tune dirty_ratio conservatively.

- PVC strategy & reclaim: use StorageClass with 'Delete' for ephemeral volumes and 'Retain' for model artifacts. Set allowedTopologies to avoid cross-rack latency.

- Networking/egress: Calico policy with egress NAT on perimeter host; for tracing and metrics, forward minimal metrics via pushgateway on jump host.

Example StorageClass snippet (RBD):
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: rbd-fast
provisioner: rook-ceph.rbd.csi.ceph.com
parameters:
  clusterID: rook-ceph
  pool: replicapool
  imageFormat: "2"
  imageFeatures: layering
reclaimPolicy: Retain
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer

Operational notes / gotchas for air-gap installs:
- Pre-seed images and operator manifests; ensure CRI supports required kernel modules (VFIO, iommu) and ensure NVIDIA drivers matched to kernel.
- Certificate management: provide an internal CA and automate cert rotation for the cluster; offline signing flow needs to be validated.
- For GPU firmware/drivers, prefer vendor-provided validated bundles to avoid kernel incompatibilities.

I'll attach a short markdown doc that compares local PV vs Rook for your specific I/O profile (storage-tiering-proposal.md).

If useful, we can include a small keystone template (systemd unit + rsync job) for the registry sync pipeline.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Maya—quick follow up and next steps: 

Thanks for the constraints doc — we've sketched the proposal above and attached the checklist. Short checklist items for the design review pack: 
- Confirm target peak GPU QPS and model sizes (weights per model).
- Confirm preferred artifact retention policy and whether cold storage offsite is acceptable.
- Provide hardware inventory (SNs + rack mapping) for GPU hosts.
- Decide on Registry sync cadence and who owns the offline transfer.

If you grant permission, I'd like to fold Marissa's storage snippets and Dylan's checklist into our onboarding runbook (we'll mark any customer-specific items as greenfield-only). Also propose a 60-minute design review Thursday 2027-03-24 10:00 PDT — please confirm availability for you and Samir.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
